definition: Autoimmunity is a state in which a person produces autoantibodies that react to the body’s own proteins. In this pregnancy-related context, maternal autoimmunity refers to such antibodies circulating in the mother and potentially affecting fetal development, including the developing brain.

reasons: The packet supports maternal autoimmunity during pregnancy and autoantibodies reactive to fetal brain proteins, but it does not support the general definition that autoimmunity is a state in which a person produces autoantibodies that react to the body’s own proteins.

The phrase 'potentially affecting fetal development, including the developing brain' goes beyond the packet’s wording by generalizing from reported associations and mechanistic investigation to a broader definitional claim.

The definition’s first sentence gives a general, textbook-level meaning of “autoimmunity” (producing autoantibodies that react to the body’s own proteins), but the packet does not provide or explicitly support this general characterization of autoimmunity; it mainly discusses maternal autoantibodies in pregnancy (MARA) and their reactivity to fetal brain proteins.

Because the packet only directly supports the pregnancy/MARA framing (autoantibodies reactive to fetal brain proteins circulating in pregnant mothers and associated with offspring autism diagnosis, with potential effects on fetal/offspring brain development), the included general definition portion is not defensibly supported.
